features.feature_value: Removed when profanity and violence were present
features.evidence_span: Profanity and violence were the things I was looking for to remove
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states the specific content cues they used to decide removal.

features.feature_value: Chose to leave posts if they lacked violence or vulgar language
features.evidence_span: If the message didn't call for violence or have vulgar language I generally chose to leave it.
features.rationale: They describe a clear conditional rule for keeping versus removing.

features.feature_value: Respected the right to express opposing viewpoints even when disagreeing
features.evidence_span: While I might not agree with both viewpoints, I respect the right' to have them.
features.rationale: They emphasize a normative stance (respecting expression) rather than agreement.

features.feature_value: Kept if posts offered points and room for discussion; removed if just name-calling/anger
features.evidence_span: if I felt that the posts were not just hating on another group/person and made some sort of point that showed maybe there was room for discussion
features.rationale: They contrast constructive discussion versus demeaning/angry content as the deciding factor.

features.feature_value: Influence from whether posts contributed to respectful political discourse
features.evidence_span: If they contributed to respectful political discourse
features.rationale: Their criterion directly references respectful discourse as the basis for decisions.

features.feature_value: Seeing posts together prompted consistent application of the same standards to both sides
features.evidence_span: Seeing the posts together encouraged me to apply the same standards to both sides and make a consistent judgment
features.rationale: They explicitly tie the paired format to applying consistent standards across perspectives.

features.feature_value: Checked whether both sides articulated positions with value vs just inflammatory talking points; factual inaccuracy reduced approval
features.evidence_span: if both sides actually articulated their position or if they were just saying inflammatory things without adding value
features.rationale: They describe evaluating substantive articulation/value and also mention difficulty due to factual inaccuracy.

features.feature_value: Reflection focused only on describing the mirror-imaging of arguments
features.evidence_span: The mirror image of the argument from the opposite perspective.
features.rationale: This participant provides almost no decision criteria beyond describing the mirror relationship.
